observedRepresentationFailures.cause: Two straight reference connectors of lengths 19.218958 and 11.99858 mm are in the nearest-neighbour pool but fail nonincident visible-edge clearance. Tiny intervening visible fragments leave the blocking edges 0.001042 and 0.01586 mm from connector endpoints. The complete known routing passes ordinary geometry and paper checks.
observedRepresentationFailures.implication: Re-ranking accepted candidates cannot restore rejected edges. This is also a deterministic graph-construction improvement opportunity.

observedRepresentationFailures.cause: A 0.000004 mm visible reference fragment is split into two duplicate self-loops after endpoint normalization; the embedded witness fails self-intersection and edge-parity validation.
observedRepresentationFailures.implication: Retained as a failed oracle case; no geometry tolerance or witness requirement was relaxed.

interpretation: The baseline is one sparse trace strategy, not the automatic application pipeline with direct fitting and retries.

The raster baseline uses the photographic simplification preset, including its 3 mm border stabilization band, on clean artwork. It is not a tuned clean-artwork tracing baseline; the oracle gap does not establish that learning is needed.
The 1% exported-image-error criterion belongs to this clean-mask experiment; it differs from the photographic acceptance gate.

Reference eligibility itself selects a subset. Eleven gallery references fail the imported geometry or image checks and three have unsupported rectangular overlap. This does not assert that the published designs are impossible.
Exact boundary variants also expose reference subdivision and otherwise unobservable anchors. Their gain cannot be attributed solely to denoising or edge ranking.

The compact oracle restricts candidate connectors to one known routing but does not provide sheet ownership to HiGHS. It still requires numerical geometry and nominal paper validation plus independent rendering.
Successful-only aggregate timings compare different case sets. Use per-case paired timing samples for speed comparisons.

solveSeconds includes model construction and in-solver validation. It excludes reference import, graph preparation, solver startup and post-solve export/render verification; this is not click-to-ready latency.
No physical assembly test, new trained model, or production engine change is included.
